Multi-agent orchestration is the emerging frontier: the top practical read, [a **Mixture of Agents** presets guide](/?date=2026-11-03&category=news#item-ce9cdb957c6f) (default preset **YAML**, **fanout modes**, reasoning effort, **fallbacks**), pairs with [official **Hermes Kanban** multi-agent profile docs](/?date=2026-11-03&category=research#item-hn-49604068) — carried from [10-27](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49604068), not a launch — [an Ask HN thread on coordinating many personal agents](/?date=2026-11-03&category=research#item-hn-50326764) showing the same coordination gap in practice, and [**MAServeBench**](/?date=2026-11-03&category=research#item-2610.40293) benchmarking multi-agent LLM serving under hierarchical collaboration workloads (useful agent-eval context, not Hermes-specific). beta hopefuls watch for seat expansion and the post-Thanksgiving/pre-Christmas full-release window; **K8s** deployers plan around both [documented gaps](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49977400); and watch Thursday's 👀 tease and how the migration meme converts — filing [**Pro/Max** support](/?date=2026-10-20&category=research#item-hn-49790991), [**Kanban**](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49604068), [**Verso**](/?date=2026-10-17&category=research#item-hn-49628094), [**Grafana**](/?date=2026-10-20&category=research#item-hn-49318128), [**ClusterMob**](/?date=2026-10-26&category=research#item-hn-50197497), [**Refine Cycle**](/?date=2026-10-28&category=research#item-hn-49606988), [**Paper Harness**](/?date=2026-10-30&category=research#item-hn-50278175), the [**K8s** gaps](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49977400), the [~**23k** backlog](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49424643), the [**OMH** launch/momentum posts](/?date=2026-10-25&category=social#item-85a24234b6f2), the [haywire thread](/?date=2026-10-27&category=research#item-hn-49916751), the [**Arduino UNO Q** recipe](/?date=2026-11-01&category=research#item-hn-49368474), and [**hermes-jekyl-hyde**](/?date=2026-11-01&category=research#item-hn-49231797) as reference (de-dup duty, nineteenth cycle running).

Release Date: November 2, 2026

Patch release. This tag rolls up the ~776 PRs merged since v0.22.5 into a stable release for the GitHub release (CLI and installers), the Microsoft Store app, Docker and Hermes Cloud. Full curated notes for this window ship with v0.23.0.


About this release
Measured at commit f0d94882e89, the window since v0.22.5 contains 3,448 non-merge commits across 4,316 changed files (+248,579 / −94,077), 776 merged PRs and 385 closed issues.

Full curated release notes for this window ship with v0.23.0, which will document everything from v0.22.0 onward — highlights, feature areas, and complete contributor credits. Nothing in this window is skipped.

Microsoft Store app: updates through the Store.

top_items.content:
You can now watch a graph engineering run from Hermes Desktop.

A big Hermes task used to mean scrolling back through the chat to find out which part was still running. Now you start it in Desktop and watch it instead. Desktop keeps the plan above the composer, and the Oh My Hermes pane on the right follows the run: each lane and the model it runs on, what's running, what failed and got repaired, and the verify step that has to pass before anything is called done. The status bar shows the same count, so a glance is enough when the pane is closed.

Oh My Hermes (OMH) is an open-source operating layer for Hermes Agent. You keep talking to Hermes the way you already do. Its graph engineering workflow turns your goal into a graph of small tasks, picks a skill and a model for each one, runs the independent ones in parallel, and checks the result before it reports back. It ships 100+ specialist skills (frontend, backend, Rust, security review, verification gates), and the router loads the ones a task needs, so you never call them by name.

It doesn't patch or replace Hermes. The Desktop pane is a plugin that comes with OMH: install, then turn it on under Capabilities → Plugins in Desktop.

The clip is the real Desktop app; the run in it is illustrative.

Github: https://t.co/g1exHwWK5E
